title: [Feature request] upgrade protobuf to 4.x
body:
### System information

1.14.1

### What is the problem that this feature solves?

packaging onnx for linux distributions require finding a set of packages that will work. With the recent (well fairly) update of protobuf to 4.x, it would be much easier if protobuf was upgraded to 4.x in onnx.
That would enable many downstream applications to be packaged properly. (currently on nixos those are just broken).

### Alternatives considered

leaving as is.

### Describe the feature

upgrade protobuf dependency to 4.x
and ideally release a minor version.

### Will this influence the current api (Y/N)?

I don't think so.

### Feature Area

unfortunately not sure.

### Are you willing to contribute it (Y/N)

No

### Notes

I'm a maintainer of some packages on nixos that depend on onnx. I don't have time to delve into the details of onnx myself unfortuenately. (just specifying this so you know it's not coming from a completely selfish background).

@reporter Thank you for the helpful details!

> it looks like I have the wrong version of abseil-cpp, do you know which version I should use ?

> I'm using latest version of protobuf so protobuf 3.24 and python packages version 4.24

Starting from Protobuf 3.22 they added abseil dependency, and probably Protobuf will need specific versions of abseil. Now in ONNX the recommend dependency versions are Protobuf v22.3 + abseil-cpp [20230125.3](https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp/tree/20230125.3). If there is no installed Protobuf in your environment, onnx will install Protobuf v22.3 + abseil-cpp 20230125.3 for you, as mentioned in https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/02a41bf1031defac78bd482328381f137ca99137/CMakeLists.txt#L230-L270.

If users need higher Protobuf version with ONNX, possibly Protobuf will need higher abseil-cpp versions. I did see there are quite a few similar [compatible issue for Protobuf + abseil](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aprotocolbuffers%2Fprotobuf+Abseil&type=issues) and I didn't find a clear supported versions map from them. According to their [source code](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/tree/v24.2/third_party), my best guess for the supported abseil version for Protobuf v24.2 would be [this patch](https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp/releases/tag/20230125.3).
